blocks.value: Many problems can be solved either recursively or iteratively (with a loop) — recursion often reads more clearly, while iteration is usually faster and uses less memory, since each recursive call needs its own space for parameters and local variables until it returns.
Compare the recursive factorial from earlier to an iterative version using a for loop — same result, without the overhead of repeated method calls:

Recursion trades some speed and memory for clarity. For most everyday code that tradeoff is fine, but for performance-critical situations (like control systems), the efficiency of iteration usually wins out.
